description: Risks of Seasonal Climate Extremes Related to ENSO is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by NOAA | Earth System Research Laboratory | Physical Sciences Division. This interactive map shows regions where the risk of having a seasonal extreme in temperature or precipitation is elevated during El Niño or La Niña conditions. Decision makers can identify areas that have an increased or decreased risk of extreme warm/cold (or dry/wet) seasons, and plan accordingly. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Extreme Cold, Extreme Heat. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
